rationale: The gold section states that `tox r -e stress` runs stress tests for race conditions in Click's test runner, matching the reference answer exactly.
The gold anchor states "Read and follow [AI_POLICY.md](AI_POLICY.md) before contributing," which directly supports the reference answer AI_POLICY.md.
The gold section states "Always run `python3 selftest.py` first" before the pytest commands, which supports the reference answer.
The gold section states that without the standard optional dependencies you can install with `uv add fastapi` instead of `uv add "fastapi[standard]"`, which matches the reference answer exactly.
The gold section states that the community "treat[s] one another with respect" and that "disagreement is no excuse for poor behavior and poor manners," which matches the reference answer.
The gold section states 'We use GitHub Discussions as the starting point for all bug reports, feature requests, and questions,' which directly supports the reference answer.

The gold anchor states the required first step is to fetch and read the skeleton document (blog.jaraco.com/skeleton/) in its entirety before reading further or making changes, and that it is the authoritative source for structure, conventions, testing, and release process, which matches the reference answer.

The section states "We use `black` as code formatter" and says to install tools like `black` from `requirements.txt` instead of running the latest version ("don't just use `uvx`"), which matches the reference answer.
The anchored CONTRIBUTING.rst section states "Since version 2.1.0 we use the versioning semantics described by SemVer," which directly supports the reference answer.

The anchor states that legal uncertainty about the copyright status and provenance of LLM-generated works means allowing LLM contributions has unpredictable consequences for the project's copyright status, which matches the reference answer.
The anchor states that "all contributors are expected to follow our Code of Conduct," while the AI Policy applies only to contributors who use LLM tools, so the reference answer matches the section.
The gold section states that `tornado/test/api_test.py` compares the public API (names and signatures) to the snapshot in `tornado/test/api.txt`, which directly supports the reference answer.

The gold section states that comments should explain what lines do and why, never what they replaced or which bug prompted them, that most lines need no comment, and that module docstrings should not be written, matching the reference answer exactly.
The gold section says "We follow the format from keepachangelog" and "Try sorting entries in descending order of impact / importance," which together support the reference answer.
The gold section states that HTTP/2 remains experimental, to install `zttp>=0.0.34` and enable it with `--http zttp --http2`, which matches the reference answer exactly.

The gold section says to prefer Merge when separate commits each have their own topic (such as refactorings or renames) because each commit is valuable on its own, matching the reference answer's examples in cases 3 and 4.

The gold section states that the pull request body should first reference the issue (e.g. "Fixes #1234") and that before/after code examples are usually recommended, which matches the reference answer.

The gold section's certification list has four bullets (author or legal right to submit, copyright or explicit legal authorization, understanding the code, and accepting full responsibility), which matches the reference answer item for item.
The anchor states that `Image.open()` takes a `formats=` argument (list/tuple of format IDs to allowlist) and that there is no `format=` parameter, which matches the reference answer exactly.
The gold section states documentation is built with Material for MkDocs and API documentation is built from docstrings using mkdocstrings, which matches the reference answer exactly.

The anchor states "Describe parameters in prose, naming them in italics like the standard library does (*include_universal*). No `:param:` lists.", which matches the reference answer's prose-with-italics requirement and its ban on `:param:` lists.
The gold section states that implementing a new feature requires that it be "mandatory to **discuss it first** on the issue tracker," which directly supports the reference answer.
The gold section states that "Starlette only requires `anyio`" and that `httpx2` is "Required if you want to use the `TestClient`", which matches the reference answer.
The gold section's checklist item states 'If you modify `curl_httpclient.py`, also run `tox -e py3-full`', which directly supports the reference answer.
The gold section states the release PR must include an update to the changelog following the keepachangelog format and a version bump (see __init__.py), matching the reference answer.

The gold section's THANKS paragraph says to keep the list sorted and make sure the name and email match the git configuration, because the file is regenerated from commit history and a mismatch may cause changes to be overwritten.

The gold section lists the kombu tracker as https://github.com/celery/kombu/issues and states that bugs for an ecosystem package should go to its relevant issue tracker, which supports the reference answer.
The anchored CONTRIBUTING.md section states that the test suite spawns testing servers on ports 8000 and 8001 and that these must not be in use, which matches the reference answer's ports and reason.
The gold section states "We push a new version of the documentation with each minor release, and we push to a `dev` path with each commit to `main`," which matches the reference answer exactly.

The gold section lists under v2.14.0 Fixes: "Call enum constructors in both validation modes by @Viicos in #13792", which directly supports the reference answer that enum constructors are now called in both validation modes.
The gold section under 0.161.1 (2026-10-22) Fixes states "Fix OpenAPI schemas for standalone nullable form unions," which matches the reference answer exactly.

The anchored item 4 says commit messages should explain why a change was made beyond "Fixes #NNNN", asking why this is the right fix and what other options were ruled out, which matches the reference answer.
The gold anchor NEWS.rst#41 states "Report build-backend import failures as pip errors instead of displaying an uncaught traceback," which directly matches the reference answer.
The gold section for starlette 1.10.0 lists as its first fix: "Parse the last URL-encoded form field when the request stream ends without an empty chunk," which matches the reference answer exactly.
The 10.3.0 (2024-04-01) entry in CHANGES.rst states "CVE-2024-28219: Use ``strncpy`` to avoid buffer overflow #7928", which matches the reference answer's CVE ID and fix.

The gold section states that `-c` now raises a usage error for a path that does not exist, is a directory, or has no loader, and that such paths were previously ignored or raised an unhandled `FileNotFoundError`, which matches the reference answer.
The gold anchor section for Version 2.3.2 states "Set ``Vary: Cookie`` header when the session is accessed, modified, or refreshed," which directly supports the reference answer Vary: Cookie.

The gold section states that the RANDOMIZE_DOWNLOAD_DELAY setting is deprecated and to 'Use the new DOWNLOAD_DELAY_JITTER setting instead' under the Scrapy 2.19.0 Deprecations heading, which matches the reference answer.

The Version 8.5.0 section states "Add built-in shell completion support for PowerShell (Windows PowerShell 5.1+ and pwsh 7+) alongside the existing bash, zsh, and fish completers," which directly supports the reference answer 8.5.0.
The anchor is the bare 5.7.0a1 'Bug Fixes' heading with no entries, so it neither names 5.7.0b1 nor mentions chord fixes, and the reference answer may be true in the 5.7.0b1 section instead.

The gold section states that httpx 0.25.1 (3rd November, 2023) added a `ValueError` raise when `Response.encoding` is set after `Response.text` has been accessed, matching the reference answer exactly.
The 0.52.1 entry states it 'Complete[s] the closing handshake on server-initiated WebSocket closes in the `websockets-sansio` and `wsproto` implementations,' which matches the reference answer.
The gold section states that SimpleAsyncHTTPClient now strips the `Authorization` and `Cookie` headers when following a redirect to a different origin, which matches the reference answer.
The gold section states under 1.8.0 Fixed: "Stop `FileResponse` transfers when the client disconnects," which directly supports the reference answer that the transfers are stopped.

The cited section is the 1.5.0 release notes listing two GZip fixes (#3419, #3420), and it never mentions thread_minimum_size, GZipResponder, or the 1.4.1 default, so it neither supports nor refutes the reference answer.

The gold section states that "Versions of Requests between v2.3.0 and v2.30.0 are vulnerable" to forwarding Proxy-Authorization headers on HTTPS redirects, and the section is the 2.31.0 release entry, which matches the fix version in the reference answer.

The anchored section is the 0.52.3 release note about updating zttp and HTTP/1.1 parsing performance, with no mention of 0.50.0, startup failures, exit codes, or the multiprocess supervisor, so the reference answer may be true elsewhere but this anchor does not support it.

The 0.54.0 release-notes section only says HTTP/2 is experimental and gives the zttp install and `--http zttp --http2` flags, with no mention of response trailers, the http.response.trailers extension, or the TE header, so it is insufficient to confirm or refute the reference answer.

The gold section states that feed URIs now only expand %(...)s parameters, keeping other percent characters as is, so percent-encoded URIs such as ones with %20 or percent-encoded FTP credentials are no longer misread as printf-style directives, which matches the reference answer.
The gold section under the heading '0.27.2 (27th August, 2024)' lists 'Reintroduced supposedly-private `URLTypes` shortcut. (#2673)' under Fixed, so the reference answer 0.27.2 is directly supported.
The gold section's first Fixes bullet states 'Add Mypy plugin workaround for dynamic models defined in functions' under v2.14.0a1, which matches the reference answer.
The gold section states that uvicorn 0.52.2 updated zttp to 0.0.22, fixing bodyless request receives and improving HTTP/1 request parsing performance, which matches the reference answer exactly.
The gold section states under 'Improved flag option handling' that Click 8.3.0 reworked the relationship between `flag_value` and `default` parameters, which matches the reference answer.

The gold section states that the Werkzeug dependency update to >= 2.2.2 "includes fixes related to the new faster router, header parsing, and the development server," which matches the reference answer's three areas.
The gold section states that StaticFileHandler 'no longer follows symlinks outside of the static root directory' under the 6.5.9 security fixes, matching the reference answer.
The gold section states "Update Werkzeug requirement to >=2.3.3 to apply recent bug fixes," which directly supports the reference answer >=2.3.3.
The gold section states "Declare support for Python 3.15" and "Support self-referential extras officially," which together match the reference answer of Python 3.15 and self-referential extras.

The gold section lists the exclusive-queues default (#10287), its revert (#10289), the transient-queue fix (#10290), and the removal of socket.timeout from reconnection conditions (#10285), all under 5.7.0a1 and tied to RabbitMQ 4.3.0 compatibility.
The gold section states that commits not properly formatted by black "will be rejected in CI", which directly supports the reference answer "They are rejected."
The anchor text matches the reference answer, but it sits under the 5.7.0a1 heading, so it does not show what 5.7.0b1 itself reverted.
The anchor section states 'Use `example.com` or any `.example` domain, never a real one, even in URLs that are never fetched,' which directly matches the reference answer.
The gold section states that any pull request fixing an existing issue without being assigned first will be automatically closed, which directly supports the reference answer.
The anchor section states "**No `Co-Authored-By:`** LLM trailers in commits or PR body," which directly supports the reference answer that such trailers are forbidden.

The gold section states 'Avoid ternary expressions (`x if cond else y`): coverage cannot measure both branches. Use an explicit `if`/`else` block instead,' which directly supports the reference answer.

The gold section supports the reference's description of the flag, but the reference omits the restriction the question asks for, which the same bullet states: it cannot be combined with --no-deps, -r, --group, or --requirements-from-script.

The gold section states "no unsolicited LLM comments / answers on discussions or issues" and that users who auto-submit LLM answers "will be banned, as fast as we see them", which matches the reference answer.

The gold section says to report privately via security@gunicorn.org or the GitHub 'Report a vulnerability' button in the Security section, and warns that public GitHub issues are open for everyone to see, which matches the reference answer.
The gold section states "Use `python3` and `python3 -m pip install` — never `python` or bare `pip`," which directly supports the reference answer.

The gold section states that "Purely agentic contributions are not accepted" and that pull requests "entirely generated by AI agents, with no meaningful human review, understanding, or oversight, will be closed," with every contribution needing to show a human has reviewed, understood, and taken responsibility for it, which matches the reference answer.
The gold section states that users who post content trolling for karma, upvotes, vanity commits, or positive responses, whether or not the content is machine generated, "will be banned."

The gold section states that requests notifies the Python Maintenance Team at Red Hat and Daniele Tricoli at Debian ahead of a public release, at least a week before the planned release date, and that the intended patch is provided to them ahead of time.
The anchor states verbatim in the TL;DR list: "DoS-by-slop leads to a permanent ban." which matches the reference answer "A permanent ban."
The gold section says to open a draft Security Advisory via GitHub and to "not disclose this to anyone else," which directly supports the reference answer.

The gold section states that a DoS report must demonstrate either an input costing substantially more CPU per byte than the ~9µs/byte baseline, or an input that blocks the event loop substantially longer than a few milliseconds, which matches the reference answer.
The anchor says that if an AI agent creates a PR or issue despite the restrictions, it must make "Generated by an AI agent: <tool>, <model>" the last line, which matches the reference answer.
The gold section states that pull requests with an LLM product listed as co-author "can't be merged and will be closed without further discussion," which matches the reference answer.
The gold section states that 'Things that **should not** go in the changelog: changes to documentation, tests or tooling,' which matches the reference answer exactly.

The section says pull requests are accepted only for issues labeled `open for pull requests`, that a PR without such a reference is closed automatically, and that for an issue with none of the listed labels, asking on the issue is fine but opening a pull request is not and will be closed.
The gold anchor states "Please do not abuse the issue tracker for support questions," which directly supports the reference answer.
The gold section states verbatim that "All Python code must follow the :pep:`8` guidelines," which directly supports the reference answer PEP 8.
The gold section states under "No AI in comments" that comments on issues and PRs must be written by the human, not by an AI tool, which supports the reference answer.

The gold section states that archived branches "are kept for preserving history only, and theoretically someone could provide patches for these if they depend on a series that's no longer officially supported."

The gold section says "Do not document deprecated features, known bugs, or implementation details such as the order in which things happen internally. Never use the `deprecated` directive." which matches the reference answer.
The gold section states "Use fully qualified exception names: `Image.DecompressionBombError` and `Image.DecompressionBombWarning`, not the bare class names," which matches the reference answer.
The gold section states that 24.4.2 is a bugfix release fixing two regressions in the new f-string parser introduced in 24.4.1, which matches the reference answer exactly.

The gold section states that Django uses Trac to keep track of bugs, feature requests, and associated patches because GitHub doesn't provide adequate tooling for its community, which matches the reference answer.

The anchored section states that "Repeated slop contributions are unacceptable, and will be closed without review" and that pip "reserve[s] the right to exclude contributors who continue to submit such material," which matches each part of the reference answer.
